newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - THAI NEWSPAPERS - AUG 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - THAI NEWSPAPERS - AUG 11.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- His Majesty the King has expressed his concern over the country's situation, as Parliament prepares for next month's debate and vote on the draft for a new constitution, a coalition leader says. Realising his corcern about possibility of untoward incidents, Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh is trying to lobby his coalition partners to support the draft. The coalition leader said that Chavalit had conveyed King Bhumibol's concern to some coalition leaders. (THE NATION)

- A group of Chiang Mai University lecturers has called on Chart Pattana, the second largest party in the coalition, to quit the government which is facing a crisis of confidence. Sixty-six university lecturers from all faculties have signed their names urging Chart Pattana, which commands 52 votes in the six-party government to leave the Chavalit Yongchaiyudh administration in order to press the prime minister to step down and allow a new government to handle the economy. (BANGKOK POST)

- An award presentation planned for a taxi driver who became a national hero after reportedly returning 800,000 baht in cash to a French passenger has been postponed and tourist police are asking for witnesses to come forward and support his story. Sompong Luedtahan, who has received public donations and appeared on TV and radio shows, identified the passenger only as "John". He said in several interviews that there were witnesses when he returned the cash and cheques and title deeds worth 18 million baht to the jubilant foreigner at the airport. (THE NATION, Bangkok POST)

- Some of the 42 suspended finance companies have started their first steps to rehabilitation by laying down plans to raise their capital in order to facilitate debt repayment to the Financial Institutions Development Fund (FIDF). (BUSINESS DAY)

- The recent disclosure of financial irregularities at Alphatec Electronics Plc has raised further doubts about the quality of auditors and auditing in Thailand. The news came just three weeks after the Commerce Ministry revoked the licences of eight auditors who claimed to have certified more than 1,000 financial statements each in a year. (BANGKOK POST)
